answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller identity to lock 100 tokens in a bond before accepting jobs, whether trading land on a knoll, freight at a wharf, or velvet. The same tokens cannot back multiple identities, and cryptographically proven double-selling forfeits the bond. Creating 1,000 active aliases therefore ties up 100,000 tokens and exposes a separate bond to loss for each cheating alias; fresh names do not reset that cost.
